content.overview: Article 153 provides that there shall be a Governor for each State. Provided that nothing in this article shall prevent the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more States.
content.glance: Each State has a Governor; the same person may be appointed Governor for two or more States.
content.study:
Article 153 is the constitutive provision for the office of Governor. One person may be Governor of more than one State. The Governor is the constitutional head of the State executive (Art 154) and acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (Art 163), subject to areas where the Constitution requires discretion.

Examination: one Governor per State; same person may cover two or more States; link Arts 154, 155, 163.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: There shall be a Governor for each State. The same person may be appointed Governor for two or more States.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 153 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 153 provides that there shall be a Governor for each State. Nothing in the article prevents the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more States.

examTips: Governor for each State; same person may hold more than one State.

keyTakeaways: Art 153: Governor for each State; dual/multi-State appointment allowed.
